newsitem.title: USA: U.N. official worried N.Korea food supply may lapse.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official worried N.Korea food supply may lapse.

text.p: The U.S. decision to donate additional food aid to North Korea was welcome news, a U.N. World Food Programme official said on Tuesday, saying there was concern whether food supplies would last until the new harvest.

Douglas Coutts, head of the agency's North American office, said North Korea's food distribution system, which provides a basic ration to two-thirds of its population, "could run out of food to distribute" by late summer.

"We are very worried," Coutts said, over whether North Korea would be able to maintain its current distribution of 100 grams to 200 grams of food per day to recipients until harvest-time in September and October.

With the decision to provide an additional $15 million of aid in the form of 50,000 metric tons of U.S. corn, the United States will provide $33 million in assistance, or one third of the $95 million requested by WFP.

"This (new donation) is very good news," Coutts told the Korea Society of Washington. His remarks to the group were interrupted by a call on his cellular phone from the State Department to announce the donation.
North Korea agreed earlier this month to a barter with Cargill Inc, in which it reportedly would trade 4,000 tons of zinc for 20,000 tons of white wheat.

"This is a sign of distress for us," Coutts said because it suggested North Korea did not have enough money to fulfil its food needs. But it also showed the chance for Pyongyang to acquire food commercially, he said.
"We're hoping commercial concerns in the trade might consider this an opportunity to get involved in North Korea," Coutts said.
